title: How do the signs change these eight answers?
description: Eight sums and differences are made from thirteen and eight with different signs. Every subtraction is turned into adding the additive inverse, then the rules for same signs and different signs give each value. The video breaks the slip of thinking that taking away a negative number must make the answer smaller.
teaching_notes: One idea: turn each subtraction into adding the additive inverse, then use the sign rules of addition. Watch for students who think subtracting a negative number makes the answer smaller.

video_script.why: The child solves eight sums and differences by turning each subtraction into adding the additive inverse.
video_script.substitution: The book's eight expressions made from 13 and 8, solved by the rule that subtraction is the addition of the additive inverse.
video_script.anchor: the grid of eight expressions of the book, two rows of four
video_script.payoff_line: The first row gives minus five, minus twenty one, minus five and minus twenty one

final_answer.spoken: minus five, minus twenty one, minus five and minus twenty one in the first row, and minus five, five, five and twenty one in the second row

never_show: the values of the eight expressions before the steps
maths_rules: subtraction is the addition of the additive inverse: 8 − 13 = 8 + (−13); (−13) − (−8) = (−13) + 8; (−8) − (−13) = (−8) + 13; 13 − (−8) = 13 + 8
video_script.design: The eight expressions of the book stay in two rows of four on the board. Each one is rewritten as an addition, grouped by the signs of its two numbers, and its value is placed under it.

<bookmark mark='sub'/>Subtracting a number is the same as adding its additive inverse.
<bookmark mark='ex'/>Seven take away minus two becomes seven plus two.

narration: <bookmark mark='change'/>Step one, turn every subtraction into an addition of the additive inverse.
<bookmark mark='ex1'/>Eight take away thirteen becomes eight plus the inverse of thirteen.
<bookmark mark='ex2'/>Minus thirteen take away minus eight becomes minus thirteen plus eight.

beats.on_screen: both numbers negative: (−8) + (−13) and (−13) + (−8); add without signs, 8 + 13 = 21, keep the minus: −21

marks.same: the two expressions with both numbers negative are picked out
marks.add: the numbers are added without signs
marks.keep: the minus is placed in front of the result

narration: <bookmark mark='same'/>Step two, two of them add two negative numbers.
<bookmark mark='add'/>Add the numbers without signs, and eight and thirteen make twenty one.
<bookmark mark='keep'/>Keep the minus on the result, so both give minus twenty one.

beats.on_screen: different signs, greater number negative: 13 − 8 = 5, keep the minus: 8 + (−13) = −5; (−13) + 8 = −5; 8 − 13 = −5

marks.diff: three expressions with different signs and the greater number negative are picked out
marks.rule: the smaller number is taken from the greater and the sign of the greater is kept

beats.removed: the expressions with both numbers negative
narration: <bookmark mark='diff'/>Step three, add numbers with different signs, such as eight and minus thirteen.
<bookmark mark='rule'/>Take the smaller number from the greater, and keep the sign of the greater.
<bookmark mark='first'/>Thirteen take away eight leaves five, and thirteen is negative, so the answer is minus five.
<bookmark mark='others'/>Minus thirteen take away minus eight gives minus five too. Eight plus minus thirteen gives minus five as well.

marks.pos: (−8) − (−13) turns into (−8) + 13 and the greater number 13 is positive
marks.five: the answer 5 is written, and 13 − 8 = 5 is written beside it
marks.last: 13 − (−8) turns into 13 + 8 and the answer 21 is written

beats.removed: the expressions with a negative result
narration: <bookmark mark='pos'/>Step four, minus eight take away minus thirteen becomes minus eight plus thirteen.
<bookmark mark='five'/>The greater number is thirteen, which is positive, so the answer is five. Thirteen take away eight is also five.
<bookmark mark='last'/>Thirteen take away minus eight becomes thirteen plus eight, which is twenty one.

marks.check: the rule starting position plus movement gives the target is written

narration: <bookmark mark='check'/>Step five, check by adding back, because starting position plus movement gives the target.
<bookmark mark='one'/>Minus eight plus minus five gives minus thirteen, which matches.
<bookmark mark='two'/>Minus eight plus twenty one gives thirteen, which matches too.
